en.name: Luffa
en.summary: Luffa is the young sponge gourd, eaten before the fibre network inside develops — the same fruit left to mature becomes a bath sponge. No figure is published for it, so treat it like summer squash: about 4–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Luffa should not be kept at room temperature. It is picked young and thin-skinned, and in a warm kitchen it loses water quickly and the flesh starts to toughen as the fibres inside develop — the gourd is still trying to become a sponge. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Refrigerate it whole and dry as soon as you get home.
en.fridge: Store luffa whole and dry in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 4–7 days is the working limit. That figure is borrowed from summer squash, which luffa resembles closely in water content and handling; nothing is published for 絲瓜 itself. Buy them heavy and firm — a light gourd is a fibrous one. The flesh browns quickly once cut, so peel and cook straight away; a cut end wrapped tightly in cling film buys you a day or two, no more.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for luffa and freezing it raw is not worth doing. It is largely water held in a very soft flesh, and what thaws is a collapsed, dripping mass — the texture that makes luffa good, that slippery tenderness, is the first thing to go. If you have too much, cook it now: luffa with egg, or luffa with clams, takes minutes and is far better than anything the freezer will give back.
spoilage: A gourd that feels light for its size, with tough fibrous flesh inside
Soft, sunken or watery patches on the skin
Flesh gone brown or spongy when cut across
Slimy skin, or mould at the stem or blossom end
tips: Choose gourds that feel heavy and firm; lightness means fibre has developed.
Peel only the ridges and the toughest skin, not the pale green flesh underneath.
Cook it the moment it is cut — luffa browns faster than an apple.
It releases a lot of water in the pan, so cook it fast and do not add stock until you see how much it gives up.

faq.q: How long does luffa last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 4–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, stored whole and dry in the crisper. That figure is borrowed from summer squash; none is published for luffa.
No timeline exists and it is not worth it. Raw luffa thaws collapsed and watery, losing the tender texture that is the reason to eat it.

faq.q: Why has my luffa gone stringy?
faq.a: It was picked or kept too long and the fibre network inside has started to develop. That is the same fibre that becomes a bath sponge, and no amount of cooking will soften it.

faq.q: Do you have to peel luffa?
faq.a: Partly. Shave off the ridges and the toughest outer skin with a peeler and leave the pale green layer underneath, which is tender and keeps the pieces from falling apart.

zh.name: 絲瓜
zh.summary: 絲瓜是趁嫩採收的瓜，要在裡面的纖維網形成之前吃掉——同一顆瓜放到老，就變成洗澡用的菜瓜布。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照夏南瓜來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 4～7 天。
zh.pantry: 絲瓜不應該放室溫。它是趁嫩採收、皮薄的瓜，在溫暖的廚房裡失水很快，瓜肉也會隨著內部纖維發育而變韌——這顆瓜其實還在努力變成菜瓜布。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請整條保持乾燥直接冷藏。
zh.fridge: 請整條保持乾燥放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 4～7 天是工作上限。這個數字是比照夏南瓜而來——兩者含水量和處理方式都很接近；絲瓜本身沒有公布的數據。挑的時候要挑沉甸甸、結實的，輕飄飄的就是已經走纖維了。瓜肉切開後褐變非常快，所以請削好就立刻下鍋；切口用保鮮膜緊貼包好大概可以多撐一兩天，不會更多。
zh.freezer: 絲瓜沒有冷凍保存期限，生凍也不值得。它基本上就是包在極軟瓜肉裡的水，解凍後只剩一灘塌掉又滴水的東西——而讓絲瓜好吃的那份滑嫩，正是第一個消失的。真的太多的話，現在就煮吧：絲瓜炒蛋、蛤蜊絲瓜，幾分鐘就好，而且遠勝冷凍庫還你的任何東西。
spoilage: 拿起來比看起來輕，切開後瓜肉纖維又粗又韌
表皮出現軟塌、凹陷或滲水的區塊
橫切後瓜肉發褐或呈海綿狀
表皮黏滑，或蒂頭、花蒂處長黴
tips: 挑沉甸甸、結實的；變輕就代表纖維已經開始發育。
只削掉稜和最外層的硬皮，底下那層淡綠的瓜肉要留著。
切好立刻下鍋——絲瓜褐變比蘋果還快。
它在鍋裡會大量出水，所以要快炒，而且先看它出多少水再決定要不要加高湯。

faq.q: 絲瓜放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、整條乾燥放在蔬果室，約 4～7 天。這個數字是比照夏南瓜而來；絲瓜本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，也不值得。生絲瓜解凍後會塌掉出水，失去它最重要的滑嫩口感。

faq.q: 絲瓜為什麼變得粗粗有纖維？
faq.a: 採收太晚或放太久，內部的纖維網已經開始形成。那就是最後會變成菜瓜布的纖維，怎麼煮都不會軟。
削一部分就好。用削皮器把稜和最外層硬皮刨掉，保留底下那層淡綠色，它很嫩，也能讓瓜塊煮的時候不散開。
